description:
Read only the profiler report from the previous task and produce an executable NAS search space plan in JSON.
Behavior requirements: - Be conservative and pragmatic. - Prefer simple, well-established model families. - Include only model families clearly supported by profiler evidence. - Use small, bounded, realistic hyperparameter ranges. - Prefer categorical choices and small discrete ranges over wide continuous spaces. - Express uncertainty when profiler evidence is incomplete.
Strict constraints: - Do not inspect raw datasets. - Do not call dataset inspection tools. - Do not train models. - Do not run Optuna. - Do not evaluate model performance. - Do not select a final model.
Output must be strict JSON only (no markdown, no code fences, no prose before/after JSON).
\n\nInput: use only the profiler report generated by the previous task.

key_constraints: Small sample size relative to dimensionality (2,660 samples vs 2,500 features)

selected_model_families.rationale: The 2,500 sequential numeric features represent an ECG signal. 1D-CNNs are effective at capturing local temporal patterns (e.g., QRS complexes) while maintaining parameter efficiency compared to dense networks.
A simple multi-layer perceptron serves as a baseline. However, given the 1:1 ratio of samples to features, aggressive regularization and small hidden layers are required to prevent memorization.

uncertainty_notes: Sampling frequency (Hz) is unknown, making it difficult to determine the optimal receptive field (kernel size).
Temporal continuity between samples is unknown; samples are assumed to be independent after deduplication.
The range of float64 values is unknown, which may necessitate a batch normalization layer in the search space if values are not pre-scaled.
handoff_notes: Deduplicate the 56 identified rows prior to training/search.
Implement early stopping with a patience of 10-20 epochs due to the risk of overfitting on the small dataset.
Use Binary Cross-Entropy as the loss function and Accuracy/F1-Score as the primary search metrics.
If CNN1D is used, ensure global average pooling is applied before the final dense layer to keep parameter counts low.
